title: Lesson 4: Close Read-aloud, Session 2 and Role-Playing: Summer Sun Risin'
objective: Students will describe what the boy and the sun do at the beginning of the story Summer Sun Risin' and demonstrate understanding through role-playing and partner discussions about respect and their experiences with the sun rising.

what_is_taught.skill: describe actions of characters and elements in a story
participate in role-playing to demonstrate understanding of story events
use partner discussion protocols to share ideas about respect and experiences
listen and respond to peers' ideas using sentence stems and paraphrasing
follow multi-step movement routines safely and accurately
use sentence frames to express ideas about respect
interpret verbal and visual cues to understand story vocabulary and meaning

what_is_NOT_taught: formal vocabulary instruction beyond contextual understanding

student_actions.oral_production: participate in partner and group discussions, role-play characters, and share ideas orally
student_actions.procedural_application: perform the Sun Movement routine steps safely and in sequence
student_actions.representation_modeling: model movements and role-play characters from the story
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain what motions represent and how respect is shown using sentence stems and paraphrasing
student_actions.comprehension_response: respond to questions about story events and partner discussions about respect and experiences with the sun rising

evidence.quote: Invite students to stand up and spread out inside and around the edge of the whole group meeting area. As needed, remind students to move safely and make space for everyone.
Model Steps 6-10 of the Sun Movement routine while referencing the Sun Movement chart:
Point to the image next to Step 6 and read aloud the step: 'Slowly stretch your body up to the right, keeping arms in line with your ears.'
Invite students to join you as you practice Steps 1-10.

Offer students specific, positive feedback on their work learning the new movements in the routine. (Example: 'I noticed that everyone took great care to make sure their bodies were safe as we learned the new movements.')

After demonstrating Steps 6-10 of the Sun Movement routine, support comprehension by asking students to share what they think the motions represent (the sunbeams are spreading light and warmth in all directions). (MMR)
I can describe what the boy and the sun do in the beginning of Summer Sun Risin'.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
Tell students that during today's close read-aloud session, they will read to meet this target.

Guide students through the close read-aloud for Summer Sun Risin' using the Close Readaloud Guide: Summer Sun Risin' (Session 2; for teacher reference). Consider using the Reading Literature Checklist during the close read-aloud(see Assessment Overview and Resources).
'What is Pa doing?' (opening the barn door a little bit)
'What is the boy doing?' (opening the barn door really wide)
'What is the sun doing?' (Shining; filling the barn with sunlight)
Refocus students whole group.
Tell students they are now going to act out part of Summer Sun Risin' using the Role-Play Protocol anchor chart. Share that acting out different parts of the text can help them understand it better.
Invite students to begin the Role-Play protocol. All students should first act out pages 3-4, then pages 5-6.

Refocus students whole group and offer them specific, positive feedback on their roleplaying. (Example: 'I noticed everyone participated and worked with their partner to act out what the boy did at the beginning of the story.')
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner:
Direct students' attention to the Working to Become Ethical People anchor chart and read the title aloud.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
Direct students' attention to the Working to Become Ethical People anchor chart. Point to the column that reads, 'What does it mean?' and read the definition of respect:

Tell students they are going to use the Think-Pair-Share protocol to discuss how they showed respect during the Role-Play protocol. Remind them that they used this protocol in Lesson 2, and review as necessary using the Think-Pair-Share Protocol anchor chart. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of this protocol.)
Invite students to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner:
Offer the following sentence stems as necessary:
Gather students back together and invite a few students to share with the whole group.
Remind students that they will keep working on what respect looks like and sounds like throughout the unit.

Gather students together whole group. Tell them that they just finished role-playing what the boy in Summer Sun Risin' experiences when the sun is rising. They now get to talk with a partner about what they experience when the sun is rising. Define experience (to feel or know).

Tell students they are going to discuss their experience when the sun is rising with a pinky partner. Remind them that they used this protocol in Module 1 and review as necessary, using the Pinky Partners anchor chart. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of this protocol.)
-Guide students through the protocol to discuss their experience when the sun is rising.

-As students talk, circulate and listen in. Take note of the ideas students are sharing and target a few students to share out with the whole group. Consider documenting progress toward using the Speaking and Listening Checklist.
Remind students to make a bridge with their arms after both partners have shared.
Gather students back together and invite a few students to share with the whole group.

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model Steps 6-10 of the Sun Movement routine while referencing the Sun Movement chart; read aloud learning targets and story chunks; model role-play protocol steps; read and explain anchor charts about respect and ethical habits; model Think-Pair-Share and Pinky Partners protocols.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: How do these pictures help us understand this learning target?
Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?
How will you show respect during our Role-Play protocol?
How does the picture on the chart show respect?
What did it look and sound like when you were showing respect during the Role-Play protocol?
Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?

notes: The lesson integrates physical movement with comprehension and social-emotional learning through respect. It supports ELLs with language scaffolds and offers sensory accommodations. The lesson emphasizes oral language production and partner collaboration.

text_complexity.quantitative: read-aloud mediation; text pages 2-10 of Summer Sun Risin'
text_complexity.qualitative: simple narrative structure with supportive illustrations; familiar language; low knowledge demands
text_complexity.reader_and_task: read-aloud removes decoding load; tasks require oral comprehension and oral production through discussion and role-play
